Obligation: Operate only under a valid Money Lender or NDT MFI licence
Source / provision: Act Parts IV and V; Guidelines 3 to 5
Recipient: Internal; UMRA where clarification is needed

guide.what: Digital lending is a way of delivering credit, not a separate licence. Keep the lending business inside the activities allowed by the licence and do not present the app or platform as independently licensed.
guide.do: Block an activity that is outside the licence until UMRA confirms the correct route.
guide.keep: Current licence, product inventory and perimeter review

Obligation: Do not collect deposits

guide.what: Do not accept customer money as a deposit or savings product. Loan repayments and permitted fees should not be presented or held as deposits.
guide.do: Product and funds-flow review before launch and after material changes.
guide.keep: Funds-flow diagram, product approval and customer terms

Obligation: Track licence conditions, directives and inspection findings

guide.what: Create a separate task for every condition on the licence and every later UMRA letter, direction or inspection finding. Use the date and wording in that document instead of guessing a deadline.
guide.do: Create a dated task on receipt, assign an owner, and keep the response and closure evidence.
guide.keep: Incoming document, action plan, response and closure confirmation

Obligation: Display the licence and licensed identity
Source / provision: Money Lenders reg.10; NDTMFI reg.12; Digital Lending Guidelines 11 and 19

guide.what: Keep the licence/regulated identity visible as required. For NDTMFIs, also keep the prescribed product/service and fee information displayed at the business premises; digital channels must show the licensed identity and business address.
guide.do: Include licence display and identity checks in branch and channel reviews.
guide.keep: Dated display photos, app screenshots and website archive

Obligation: Maintain at least one registered physical office

guide.what: Keep a real, registered office where the licensed lender can be contacted. State that address clearly in the app, website and other digital channels.
guide.do: Verify the office and published address quarterly and before renewal.
guide.keep: Lease or ownership record, registered address and screenshots

Obligation: Keep directors, chief executive and significant shareholders fit and proper

guide.what: Screen new and existing controllers and senior leaders for integrity, competence and financial soundness. Escalate any event that could affect their suitability.
guide.do: Do not appoint or retain a person where the required UMRA clearance has not been obtained.
guide.keep: Declarations, checks, fit-and-proper forms and UMRA decision

Obligation: Obtain written approval before changing management
Source / provision: Money Lenders regs.7 to 8; NDT MFI reg.22

guide.what: Do not change directors or management until UMRA has completed its review and issued written authorisation or a notice of no objection.
guide.do: Block the appointment and Companies Registry filing until the approval is attached.
guide.keep: Board papers, fit-and-proper pack and UMRA approval

Obligation: Obtain approval before amalgamation or transfer of assets and liabilities
Legal clock: Before signing or implementing the arrangement

guide.what: Do not merge or transfer all or part of the lending business, assets or liabilities to another entity until UMRA has approved the arrangement in writing.
guide.do: Make regulatory approval a transaction condition and keep the approval with the closing file.
guide.when: Before signing or implementing the arrangement
guide.keep: Transaction papers, customer-impact plan and UMRA approval

Obligation: Notify UMRA and pay the required fee before a Money Lender uses an additional place
Legal clock: Before business starts at the place

guide.what: A Money Lender that wants another physical place of business must notify UMRA and pay the inspection and registration fee before operating there.
guide.do: Block opening until notification, payment and registration evidence are complete.
guide.when: Before business starts at the place
guide.keep: Notice, payment receipt, inspection record and updated licence information

Obligation: Obtain prior written approval before an NDT MFI opens a branch or outlet

guide.what: An NDT MFI must not open a branch or operating outlet until UMRA has approved it in writing.
guide.do: Block premises launch and customer activity until written approval is retained.
guide.keep: Business case, application and written approval

Obligation: Renew the annual licence before expiry
Legal clock: Money Lender: at least 3 months before 31 December; NDTMFI: at least 90 days before 31 December
Source / provision: Money Lenders reg.11; NDT MFI reg.8

guide.what: The licence runs to 31 December each year. Submit a complete renewal pack and the prescribed fee early enough for continuity. Money Lender applications are due at least three months before expiry; NDTMFI applications are due at least ninety days before expiry.
guide.do: FITSPA Compliance Platform derives 31 December and calculates the legal renewal date by route; it does not ask the user to enter a licence-expiry date.
guide.when: Money Lender — at least 3 months before 31 December. NDTMFI — at least 90 days before 31 December.
guide.keep: Renewal form, supporting documents, fee receipt, submission proof and renewed licence

Obligation: Pay the annual licence fee with the renewal
Source / provision: Act ss.63 and 81; 2018 Regulations fee schedules

guide.what: Pay the prescribed annual fee when applying for renewal. Failure to pay can lead to cancellation of the licence.
guide.do: Create one controlled renewal workflow for the form, supporting pack and fee receipt.
guide.keep: Payment instruction, receipt and renewal submission

Obligation: Commence and continue the licensed business
Legal clock: NDT: within 6 months; Money Lender: within 12 months

guide.what: An NDT MFI risks revocation if it does not start or stops business within six months of licence issue. A Money Lender risks revocation if it does not start within twelve months or ceases the licensed business.
guide.do: Monitor go-live and inactivity, and seek written direction before the limit is reached.
guide.when: NDT: within 6 months; Money Lender: within 12 months
guide.keep: Go-live evidence, activity reports and UMRA correspondence

Obligation: Provide books, records and information requested by UMRA
Legal clock: Date and format stated by UMRA

guide.what: Keep the records in a form that can be produced promptly. Treat each inspection or information request as a controlled submission with a named owner and a complete copy of what was shared.
guide.do: Create the task from the request and retain the submitted version and receipt.
guide.when: Date and format stated by UMRA
guide.keep: Request log, approved response, documents supplied and receipt

Obligation: Notify MRD-MoFPED of material changes to information supplied for the licence
Legal clock: On occurrence/alteration; specific changes may have a more precise clock

guide.what: When an event or alteration materially affects information supplied or required during the licence application, the Money Lender must give written notice.
guide.do: Open a material-change workflow when the change is approved internally; apply the specific legal clock where one exists.
guide.when: On occurrence/alteration; specific changes may have a more precise clock
guide.keep: Change approval, notice, delivery proof and updated regulator record

Obligation: Notify a Money Lender address change within seven days

guide.what: A Money Lender must maintain a physical address and notify the regulator when the address changes.
guide.do: Start the seven-day clock from the effective address change and retain delivery/update evidence.
guide.keep: Internal address-change approval, notice, delivery proof and updated regulator particulars

Obligation: Reconcile a borrower account when the borrower deposits repayment with the regulator
Legal clock: As required by the regulator notice

guide.what: If a borrower deposits repayment with the regulator because payment to the lender was refused or impracticable, the lender must respond to the regulator notice, receive the money and reconcile the borrower account.
guide.do: Create the occurrence from the incoming notice; record receipt of funds and account reconciliation.
guide.when: As required by the regulator notice
guide.keep: Regulator notice, receipt of funds, account reconciliation and customer record

Obligation: Safeguard collateral in custody and compensate for loss, damage or destruction as required
Applies to: Money Lender - if collateral is held in custody
Legal clock: Prudent care at all times; compensation within a reasonable time after loss/damage event

guide.what: A Money Lender holding collateral must exercise prudent care. If collateral is lost, damaged or destroyed, the lender has a compensation obligation under the regulation.
guide.do: Maintain custody controls. A loss/damage event opens an assessment and compensation workflow; do not invent a fixed statutory day.
guide.when: Prudent care at all times; compensation within a reasonable time after loss/damage event
guide.keep: Custody register, condition records, incident assessment, valuation and compensation evidence

Obligation: Provide Money Lender transaction information requested by a borrower
Legal clock: No fixed period stated in reg.25

guide.what: A borrower may request information about the money-lending transaction, including principal outstanding, interest payable and payments received.
guide.do: Open a customer-request workflow on receipt and use a prompt internal service target without presenting it as a statutory deadline.
guide.when: No fixed period stated in reg.25
guide.keep: Request, account extract, approved response and delivery proof

Obligation: Notify the borrower of a Money Lender debt assignment within five days
Legal clock: Within 5 days from the date of assignment

guide.what: When a Money Lender assigns a debt, the borrower must receive the prescribed notice identifying the assignee.
guide.do: Start the five-day clock from the assignment date and use the prescribed Form 8 notice.
guide.when: Within 5 days from the date of assignment
guide.keep: Assignment record, Form 8 notice and delivery proof

Obligation: Compute Money Lender interest on the monthly outstanding principal balance and disclose the method
Legal clock: At calculation and before/through customer disclosure

guide.what: Money Lender interest is computed on the monthly outstanding principal balance after principal repayments, and the method must be disclosed to the borrower.
guide.do: Validate the calculation method in the product and contract; sample-test calculations and disclosures.
guide.when: At calculation and before/through customer disclosure
guide.keep: Pricing formula, contract disclosure, test cases and reconciliation

Obligation: Respond to a Money Lender notice of intended revocation within fourteen days

guide.what: If the regulator serves a notice of intention to revoke the Money Lender licence, the lender has fourteen days to show cause in writing.
guide.do: Create a critical regulator-response occurrence immediately on receipt and preserve the received timestamp.
guide.keep: Received notice, response, supporting evidence and delivery receipt

Obligation: Classify the NDTMFI loan portfolio using the prescribed performance categories

guide.what: NDTMFI loans must be classified into the prescribed performing, watch, substandard, doubtful and loss categories using the regulatory delinquency criteria.
guide.do: Run the classification logic continuously and reconcile it at each quarter end before the regulatory return.
guide.keep: Loan ageing, classification report, exception log and quarter-end reconciliation

Obligation: Suspend accrued interest on prescribed NDTMFI non-performing classifications and observe the accrued-interest limit

guide.what: For substandard, doubtful and loss loans, the NDTMFI must apply the regulatory treatment for accrued interest and observe the prescribed cap.
guide.do: System rules should automatically change interest recognition when the loan enters the relevant classification and flag breaches of the portfolio-level limit.
guide.keep: Interest suspense ledger, classification report, portfolio calculation and exceptions

Obligation: Maintain NDTMFI loan-loss allowances at the prescribed classification percentages
Legal clock: At all times and reflected at reporting dates

guide.what: The NDTMFI must provide at least the prescribed loan-loss allowance for each regulatory loan classification.
guide.do: Calculate regulatory provisioning from the classified portfolio and reconcile it to finance records before each return and financial close.
guide.when: At all times and reflected at reporting dates
guide.keep: Provision calculation, GL reconciliation, approvals and exceptions

Obligation: Maintain NDTMFI collateral charges, insurance and an updated collateral register
Legal clock: Before reliance on the security and while held

guide.what: Where an NDTMFI takes collateral, it must ensure the security is properly charged, adequately insured where required, and recorded in an updated collateral register.
guide.do: Block secured-loan completion where required charge/insurance evidence is missing; monitor expiries and register updates.
guide.when: Before reliance on the security and while held
guide.keep: Security registration/charge, insurance, collateral register and review evidence

Obligation: Write off NDTMFI loans when the regulatory write-off criteria are met
Legal clock: When regulatory write-off criteria are met

guide.what: The NDTMFI must apply the regulatory write-off treatment where legal rights are lost, the debt is uncollectible, there is no realistic recovery, or the loan remains non-performing beyond the prescribed period.
guide.do: Create a write-off case from the portfolio classification; require approval and accounting treatment, and separately track recoveries after write-off.
guide.when: When regulatory write-off criteria are met
guide.keep: Write-off assessment, approval, accounting entry and recovery record

Obligation: Submit an NDTMFI corrective-action report after an inspection
Legal clock: Within 30 days after receipt of the inspection report

guide.what: After receiving the regulator inspection report, the NDTMFI must submit a corrective-action report addressing the findings.
guide.do: Open a corrective-action occurrence on receipt, map each finding to owner/action/evidence, and submit the approved report within 30 days.
guide.when: Within 30 days after receipt of the inspection report
guide.keep: Inspection report, corrective-action plan/report, evidence pack and submission receipt

Obligation: Monitor NDTMFI prudential warning conditions that may trigger regulatory management action
Source / provision: Tier 4 Act management/takeover provisions; NDTMFI Regulations, 2018 reg.25

guide.what: The NDTMFI should monitor the regulatory indicators of unsound financial condition, including the capital-to-assets condition specified in the takeover provisions. This is not an initial minimum-capital rule.
guide.do: Monitor the statutory warning indicators and escalate deteriorating positions before a supervisory trigger is reached.
guide.keep: Capital/asset calculations, liquidity/creditor monitoring, board packs and remediation plans

Obligation: Obtain prior written approval before relocating an NDTMFI place of business

guide.what: An NDTMFI must obtain regulator approval before relocating a place of business and provide the information required for the relocation application.
guide.do: Block move/go-live until written approval is attached; keep customer-transfer/liability and new-location information with the case.
guide.keep: Relocation application, supporting plan and written approval

Obligation: Obtain approval and complete the prescribed notice/reporting steps before closing an NDTMFI place of business
Legal clock: Approval before closure; public notice at least 90 days before closure; report closure within 14 days after closure

guide.what: Closing an NDTMFI place of business is a regulated workflow requiring prior approval, public notice and a post-closure regulator report.
guide.do: Create one closure case with three gates: approval, 90-day customer/public notice, and 14-day post-closure report.
guide.when: Approval before closure; public notice at least 90 days before closure; report closure within 14 days after closure
guide.keep: Approval, public notice, closure evidence and post-closure report receipt

Obligation: Submit NDT MFI quarterly risk-classification return
Legal clock: Before the 15th day of the following month

guide.what: At each quarter end, classify the loan portfolio and calculate provisions using the prescribed categories, then submit the return before the fifteenth day of the next month.
guide.do: Quarter end to the next month's 15th. Use an earlier internal review date.
guide.when: Before the 15th day of the following month
guide.keep: Approved return, portfolio reconciliation, submission proof and receipt

Obligation: Submit NDT MFI annual report and audited financial statements
Legal clock: Annually; in any case not later than 31 March of the following year

guide.what: Submit the NDTMFI annual report and audited financial statements annually, with the management structure and any other information required by the regulator.
guide.do: Plan audit and approvals early, but keep the statutory outer filing date distinct from internal preparation dates.
guide.when: In any case not later than 31 March of the following year.
guide.keep: Signed audited statements, annual report, management structure, submission proof and receipt

Obligation: Submit other UMRA returns and reports as specified

guide.what: The reporting templates show the data UMRA may collect, including financial, loan-performance and market-conduct information. The source set does not state one universal filing day for every template, so use the date in the portal, licence, notice or current reporting instruction.
guide.do: Do not turn a template into an invented monthly or quarterly deadline. Configure the task from the current instruction.
guide.keep: Completed return, source reconciliation, submission proof and receipt

Obligation: Submit the annual complaints report
Legal clock: From FCP effective date: by end of one month after the fiscal-year reporting period
Source / provision: FCP Guidelines 2019 commencement + annual complaints report provision

guide.what: Report complaints received, resolved, outstanding and referred to the regulator for the fiscal year, excluding complaints resolved by the end of the next business day as the guideline directs.
guide.do: Apply this workflow only once the FCP Guidelines are effective, calculated from the date first licensed by MRD-MoFPED; set the due date one month after the fiscal-year period ends.
guide.when: From FCP effective date — by end of one month after the fiscal-year reporting period.
guide.keep: Approved Appendix A report, complaints reconciliation, submission proof and receipt

Obligation: Retain Money Lender records for ten years

guide.what: Keep loan agreements, ledgers, cash records, security registers, debtor records and related evidence for at least ten years, with reliable retrieval and protection against alteration.
guide.do: Calculate retention record by record and pause destruction where there is a complaint, investigation or litigation hold.
guide.keep: Retention schedule, archive logs and retrieval tests

Obligation: Retain NDT MFI loan records for ten years and accounting books for at least seven years
Legal clock: Loan records: 10 years; accounting books: at least 7 years

guide.what: Use the longer ten-year period for loan-transaction files. Keep proper accounting books for at least seven years and make them available for inspection.
guide.do: Map every record class to the correct period and keep legal holds separate from ordinary retention.
guide.when: Loan records: 10 years; accounting books: at least 7 years
guide.keep: Retention schedule, archive logs, accounting records and retrieval tests

Obligation: Keep total annual interest, fees and charges within the 100 percent ceiling
Legal clock: Before offer and throughout the loan

guide.what: Across a year, the customer's total interest, fees, charges and commissions must not exceed the principal advanced. Build the ceiling into the pricing engine and test the full customer cost, not only the headline interest rate.
guide.do: Reject pricing or collections that would push total annual cost above the principal.
guide.when: Before offer and throughout the loan
guide.keep: Pricing model, test cases, approvals and exception report

Obligation: Apply the 2.8 percent monthly interest cap to Money Lender loans
Legal clock: Before offer and throughout the loan
Source / provision: Legal Notice 21 of 2024 under Act s.89

guide.what: A licensed Money Lender must not charge more than 2.8 percent interest per month. This cap is specific to Money Lenders and should not be applied to an NDT MFI without a separate legal basis.
guide.do: Validate the monthly rate separately from the broader total-cost ceiling.
guide.when: Before offer and throughout the loan
guide.keep: Pricing configuration, test cases and approved product sheet

Obligation: Limit default interest and charge it only on outstanding principal

guide.what: A default penalty rate must not exceed half of the monthly interest rate and must be charged only on the remaining principal, not on interest or fees.
guide.do: Test delinquency formulas and block interest-on-interest.
guide.keep: System rule, sample recalculation and exception report

Obligation: Do not compound interest

guide.what: Calculate interest on the monthly outstanding principal after principal repayments. Do not charge interest on accrued interest, fees or penalties.
guide.do: Reconcile system calculations to an independent sample each month.
guide.keep: Product formula, sample calculation and reconciliation

Obligation: Apply the non-performing-loan recovery cap

guide.what: Once a loan is non-performing, cap the recoverable amount at the outstanding principal plus contractual interest, fees and charges that do not exceed that principal, plus permitted recovery expenses.
guide.do: Freeze the NPL balance components and prevent later charges from exceeding the cap.
guide.keep: NPL calculation, system rule and exception report

Obligation: Give a price schedule before advancing the loan

guide.what: Before disbursement, show the interest, fees, charges and commissions that the customer may pay. Explain any non-standard, additional or third-party charge before it is incurred.
guide.do: The customer must be able to review the full price before accepting the loan.
guide.keep: Offer screen, price schedule, acceptance log and version archive

Obligation: Display standard interest rates, fees and charges on every channel

guide.what: Keep current pricing visible at branches, websites, apps and other digital channels. Update all channels together when an approved price changes.
guide.do: Use a controlled price source and archive each published version.
guide.keep: Screenshots, branch display photos, approved price list and change log

Obligation: Obtain customer consent before changing terms and UMRA approval before increasing interest

guide.what: Do not vary a loan agreement or increase charges without the customer's written consent. Do not increase the interest rate until UMRA has approved the change in writing.
guide.do: Block configuration and customer notice until the required approvals and consents are recorded.
guide.keep: Change paper, customer consent, UMRA approval and release record

Obligation: Assess the customer's ability to repay before lending

guide.what: Use reliable income, obligations, repayment history and affordability information to decide whether the customer can repay without unreasonable hardship. A score alone is not evidence unless the inputs and decision rule are understood and tested.
guide.do: No loan may proceed without a recorded affordability decision and any approved override.
guide.keep: Application data, affordability result, score, decision and override approval

Obligation: Use a complete written or electronic lending contract
Source / provision: Act ss.70 and 85; Lending Conditions reg.5

guide.what: The contract should clearly state the parties, principal, disbursement date, repayment schedule, interest method and annual rate, total cost, all fees, cooling-off right, collateral, recovery terms, guarantor terms, early repayment right and consequences of default or termination.
guide.do: Use a controlled template and prevent disbursement when mandatory fields are missing.
guide.keep: Approved template, completed contract, acceptance record and witness evidence

Obligation: Give the customer a copy of the complete agreement
Source / provision: Money Lenders reg.17(1)(a); Lending Conditions reg.5

guide.what: Provide the signed or accepted agreement and every annexure in a form the customer can retain and retrieve.
guide.do: Record successful delivery and provide a resend route.
guide.keep: Delivered contract, delivery log and resend history

Obligation: Submit the loan-agreement template at licence application and renewal
Legal clock: With the application or renewal pack

guide.what: Include the current lending-contract template in the licensing or renewal pack. If the product has changed, submit the version actually used in production.
guide.do: Reconcile the submitted template to the live app and product catalogue before filing.
guide.when: With the application or renewal pack
guide.keep: Version-controlled template, channel copy and submission proof

Obligation: Give the statutory cooling-off period and apply only the permitted administration charge
Legal clock: 5 working days for cooling off; no early-settlement charge

guide.what: Give the borrower the cooling-off period required by the Lending Conditions Regulations and ensure any administration charge for exercising the right stays within the prescribed limit.
guide.do: Build the cooling-off expiry into the agreement and workflow; do not confuse this with early settlement.
guide.when: 5 working days for cooling off; no early-settlement charge
guide.keep: Approved agreement, cooling-off calculation, disclosure and any administration-charge evidence

Obligation: Explain the guarantor's potential liability and obtain consent

guide.what: Before relying on a guarantor, explain in writing what the guarantor may have to pay and obtain written or authenticated electronic consent.
guide.do: Do not treat a contact number as consent. Keep the notice and the guarantor's acceptance.
guide.keep: Guarantor notice, consent, identity check and delivery evidence

Obligation: Issue a receipt for every transaction

guide.what: Send a hard-copy receipt, electronic receipt or instant message whenever the customer pays, receives funds or completes another loan transaction. It should identify the amount, date and transaction.
guide.do: Monitor failed receipt delivery and allow the customer to retrieve the receipt later.
guide.keep: Receipt record, delivery log and exception report

Obligation: Allow early settlement without an extra early-settlement charge

guide.what: A borrower who settles the loan before the due date should not be charged an additional amount solely for paying early.
guide.do: Calculate the settlement amount without an extra early-settlement charge and retain the calculation.
guide.keep: Settlement quote, calculation, payment record and closure statement

Obligation: Never take prohibited identity or account-access items as collateral
Source / provision: Money Lenders reg.18; Lending Conditions reg.8

guide.what: Do not take national IDs, passports, warrant cards, ATM cards, PINs, deposit books, blank cheques or pre-signed transfer instruments as security for a loan.
guide.do: Use a collateral-type allowlist and reject prohibited items.
guide.keep: Collateral register, photographs, valuation and exception report

Obligation: Give at least sixty days' written demand before selling collateral
Legal clock: At least 60 days after written demand
Source / provision: Money Lenders reg.18(3); Lending Conditions reg.9

guide.what: A lender may not sell collateral until sixty days have passed after a written demand requiring payment of the outstanding loan.
guide.do: Record the demand-delivery date and block sale before day sixty.
guide.when: At least 60 days after written demand
guide.keep: Demand notice, delivery evidence and sale-authorisation calculation

Obligation: Value collateral, apply sale proceeds correctly and preserve redemption
Source / provision: Money Lenders reg.18(4) to (8); Lending Conditions reg.9

guide.what: Before sale, obtain the required valuation and forced-sale value. Apply proceeds to the loan and proper sale expenses, return any balance, and allow the borrower to redeem before sale.
guide.do: Use a sale checklist with valuation, approval, proceeds waterfall and borrower balance payment.
guide.keep: Valuation, auction or treaty record, proceeds statement and borrower payment

Obligation: Do not threaten, shame, harass or contact the customer's phone list
Source / provision: Lending Conditions reg.13; Digital Guidelines 15; UMRA Circular 31 May 2024

guide.what: Collections staff and agents must not use violence, threats, abusive language, social-media shaming, unsolicited contact-list calls or messages, or other oppressive tactics.
guide.do: Monitor communications, investigate complaints and suspend agents who breach the rule.
guide.keep: Approved scripts, call logs, message samples, monitoring results and complaints

Obligation: Tell the borrower who the recovery agent is before contact
Applies to: Both - if third-party recovery agent/service provider is used
Legal clock: Before the agent contacts the borrower

guide.what: Give the borrower the assigned recovery agent's name and contact details by email or SMS before that agent contacts the borrower. At sanction, identify the approved agents who may be used if the loan defaults.
guide.do: Agent access and dialing remain blocked until customer notification is delivered.
guide.when: Before the agent contacts the borrower
guide.keep: Agent roster, assignment, customer notice and delivery log

Obligation: Remain accountable for recovery agents and service providers
Applies to: Both - if third-party recovery agent/service provider is used

guide.what: Use due diligence, clear contracts, training and monitoring so third parties follow the same privacy, disclosure and fair-treatment rules as the licensed lender.
guide.do: Suspend access where due diligence, training or monitoring evidence is missing.
guide.keep: Due diligence, contract, training, monitoring and remediation

Obligation: Obtain consent before sharing credit information

guide.what: Put a clear consent clause in the loan agreement and capture authentic oral, written or electronic consent before sending a customer's information to the prescribed credit-reference mechanism.
guide.do: No credit-reporting record may be sent without linked consent evidence.
guide.keep: Consent clause, consent log and reporting record

Obligation: Send complete and accurate positive and negative credit information
Legal clock: Per current credit-reference mechanism / regulator reporting arrangement

guide.what: Validate identity, balance, status and dates before reporting. Correct errors promptly and keep the source-to-submission reconciliation.
guide.do: Do not hard-code a 30-day legal deadline unless the current regulator/credit-reference instruction expressly sets it. Create the reporting occurrence from the active reporting arrangement.
guide.when: Per current credit-reference mechanism / regulator reporting arrangement
guide.keep: Submitted file, validation results, reconciliation and correction log

Obligation: Operate a free and accessible complaints mechanism

guide.what: Give customers clear channels for complaints, publish the process and escalation route, and keep a complete record of the issue, investigation, decision and remedy.
guide.do: Open a case for every expression of dissatisfaction that may involve loss, inconvenience or distress.
guide.keep: Complaints procedure, channel screenshots, case file and outcome

Obligation: Resolve complaints within the applicable regulatory clock
Legal clock: Before FCP effective date: within 30 days. From FCP effective date: final response by end of 2 weeks, subject to permitted pause.
Source / provision: Digital Lending Guidelines 2024 guideline 17(2); FCP Guidelines 2019 commencement + complaints handling time-limit provision

guide.what: Digital Lending Guidelines require a complaint to be addressed within 30 days. Once the 2019 Financial Consumer Protection Guidelines apply to the institution, they require the final response by the end of two weeks, subject to the stated information-request pause.
guide.do: Calculate FCP effective date as one year after licence issue. Use the Digital Lending 30-day clock before that date; once FCP applies, use the FCP two-week final-response clock and preserve the permitted pause when the complainant delays requested information.
guide.when: Before FCP effective date: within 30 days. From FCP effective date: final response by end of 2 weeks, subject to permitted pause.
guide.keep: Receipt timestamp, investigation, final response and customer acceptance

Obligation: Acknowledge complaints promptly and track recurring causes
Legal clock: From FCP effective date: prompt acknowledgement unless resolved within 3 business days
Source / provision: FCP Guidelines 2019 commencement + complaints handling acknowledgement/systemic-problem provisions

guide.what: Send a written or electronic acknowledgment unless the complaint is resolved within three business days. Analyse repeat complaints and fix the underlying product, process or agent problem.
guide.do: Activate the acknowledgement rule one year after licence issue. Track acknowledgement, root cause, remedy and accepted closure separately.
guide.when: From FCP effective date: prompt acknowledgement unless resolved within 3 business days
guide.keep: Acknowledgment, complaints log, root-cause report and remediation

Obligation: Provide a plain-language key facts summary before the customer commits

guide.what: Summarise the loan amount, total cost, rate basis, all fees, due dates, cooling-off right, default consequences, complaint route and important risks in a short form the customer can understand and retain.
guide.do: Do not hide key costs in linked terms. Record the version shown and accepted.
guide.keep: Approved key facts statement, screen archive and acceptance log

Obligation: Keep advertising accurate, complete and responsible
Source / provision: FCP Guidelines 8(6); Digital Guidelines 21; UMRA Circular

guide.what: Do not claim approvals, benefits, status or prices that are not true. If an advert mentions a rate or cost, show the total cost of credit clearly and state whether the rate is monthly or annual.
guide.do: Require compliance approval, archive the published version and remove misleading content immediately.
guide.keep: Approval, final advert, channel archive and withdrawal record

Obligation: Use clear language and disclose regulated status

guide.what: Keep information current, easy to find and written clearly. Use English or an appropriate official language, explain orally where needed, and show the licensed identity and UMRA-regulated status on websites, apps, adverts and documents.
guide.do: Review customer journeys and live channel content against the approved source each quarter.
guide.keep: Content standard, translations, screenshots, oral-explanation record and reviews

Obligation: Provide loan-account statements at the frequency and through the mode agreed with the customer
Source / provision: FCP Guidelines 2019, Statements of Deposit and Loan Accounts provision

guide.what: Once the Financial Consumer Protection Guidelines apply, customers with a loan account should receive statements showing balance changes, payments, disbursements and costs, at an agreed frequency and communication mode.
guide.do: Store the agreed frequency/mode in the product or account record and generate the customer statement occurrence from that agreement.
guide.keep: Statement preference, generated statement and delivery evidence

Obligation: Give the required customer notice before changes to terms, fees, charges, services or premises
Legal clock: At least 30 days before implementing the specified change; preserve separate immediate/interest-rate notice rule in FCP and prior-approval/consent rules
Source / provision: FCP Guidelines 2019, Notice of Changes provision; Digital Lending Guidelines 22; Lending Conditions Regulations reg.6

guide.what: Once the FCP Guidelines apply, customers must receive advance notice of specified changes. Interest-rate changes are also subject to the separate customer-consent and regulator-approval controls under the Digital Lending Guidelines/Lending Conditions Regulations.
guide.do: Route the change through regulatory approval/consent first where required, then schedule the FCP customer notice. Do not let the customer-notice rule replace a prior-approval rule.
guide.when: At least 30 days before implementing the specified change; preserve separate immediate/interest-rate notice rule in FCP and prior-approval/consent rules
guide.keep: Change approval, regulator approval where required, customer notice and delivery evidence

Obligation: Give fourteen days notice before closing a customer account unless a stated exception applies
Legal clock: 14 days notice, unless the stated exception applies
Source / provision: FCP Guidelines 2019, Closing of Accounts provision

guide.what: Once the FCP Guidelines apply, a provider should not close a consumer account without fourteen days notice except for the stated criminal-activity or threatening/intimidating/violent-behaviour exceptions.
guide.do: Create the closure occurrence, check whether a regulatory exception is documented, otherwise calculate 14 days from receipt of notice.
guide.when: 14 days notice, unless the stated exception applies
guide.keep: Closure reason, exception assessment where relevant, notice and delivery proof

Obligation: Maintain fair-treatment controls across products, staff and agents
Source / provision: FCP Guidelines 2019 Fairness Principle; Digital Lending consumer-protection provisions

guide.what: The FCP framework requires fair and reasonable treatment and prohibits practices such as unfair/deceptive/aggressive conduct, bribery, discrimination, undue influence and concealment of material information.
guide.do: Use policy, training, monitoring, complaints and QA evidence; open exceptions for identified conduct failures.
guide.keep: Conduct policy, training, QA samples, complaints trend and remediation

Obligation: Apply suitability controls where the lender gives personal advice or recommendations
Applies to: Both - if personal advice/recommendations are given
Source / provision: FCP Guidelines 2019, Suitability of Advice provision

guide.what: Where the provider gives advice or a personal recommendation, the FCP Guidelines require the advice to be suitable for the consumer and supported by sufficient customer information and records.
guide.do: Only trigger where the customer journey contains advice. Capture suitability information, recommendation rationale and conflict disclosures.
guide.keep: Customer information, suitability assessment, recommendation record and conflict disclosure

Obligation: Use secure, authorised lending applications

guide.what: Use systems that protect customer information and transaction integrity. Use only applications authorised by UMRA, keep the trading name tied to the licensed company and do not run duplicate apps offering the same product.
guide.do: Release remains blocked until security, identity and regulatory checks pass.
guide.keep: Architecture, security tests, release approval, app-store listing and incident log

Obligation: Do not access customer contacts, frequent calls or messages for KYC or collections

guide.what: Design the app so it cannot read or use the customer's contact list, frequently dialed contacts or phone messages to verify identity or collect a debt.
guide.do: Automated mobile-permission checks must fail a release that requests prohibited access.
guide.keep: Permission inventory, source-code review, app-store declaration and test results

Obligation: Keep customer information confidential and use it only for lawful purposes
Source / provision: Money Lenders reg.24; Digital Guidelines 9; DPPA principles

guide.what: Limit access and sharing to the purpose explained to the customer, a lawful requirement or valid consent. Apply the rule to directors, staff, agents and technology providers during and after their engagement.
guide.do: Use role-based access, confidentiality terms, monitoring and privacy review for every new use.
guide.keep: Data inventory, access logs, consent, contracts and privacy assessment

Obligation: Maintain a current PDPO registration

guide.what: A lender that controls, collects or processes personal data must be registered with the Personal Data Protection Office unless a valid exemption applies. The certificate is valid for twelve months.
guide.do: Store the certificate expiry in the dashboard and begin renewal before the statutory lead date.
guide.keep: Application, certificate, payment receipt and register extract

Obligation: Apply to renew PDPO registration at least three months before expiry

guide.what: Submit the renewal application and fee early enough to keep the registration continuous.
guide.do: Certificate expiry minus three calendar months. Enter the actual expiry date on Dashboard.
guide.keep: Renewal form, fee receipt, submission proof and renewed certificate

Obligation: Notify PDPO of registered-detail changes within fourteen days

guide.what: Tell PDPO in writing when a registered name, address, data category, processing purpose, security measure, data-protection officer or other registered particular changes.
guide.do: Change approval opens a fourteen-day notification task and evidence check.
guide.keep: Change record, notice, delivery proof and updated register evidence

Obligation: Notify PDPO immediately of unauthorised access or acquisition of personal data

guide.what: When personal data has been accessed or acquired by an unauthorised person, notify the data-protection authority immediately and state the remedial action. Also assess whether UMRA and affected customers must be notified.
guide.do: Escalate at detection, preserve the exact occurrence and discovery times, and do not wait for the full investigation before the initial notice.
guide.keep: Incident record, assessment, notices, updates and closure report

Obligation: Answer access requests within thirty days

guide.what: After verifying identity, give the customer the personal data and required information that can lawfully be disclosed, or explain the lawful reason for refusal.
guide.do: Start the clock on receipt, verify identity without unnecessary delay and record redactions.
guide.keep: Request, identity check, search log, response and delivery proof

Obligation: Respond to an objection to harmful processing within fourteen days

guide.what: When a customer asks the lender to stop processing that causes or is likely to cause unwarranted substantial damage or distress, respond in writing within fourteen days with compliance or the reasons for not complying.
guide.do: Route the notice immediately to the DPO and prevent silent expiry.
guide.keep: Notice, assessment, decision, response and system action

Obligation: Delete, destroy or de-identify data when lawful retention ends
Legal clock: At expiry, after holds and legal duties are checked

guide.what: Do not keep personal data longer than needed unless law, contract, consent or another lawful ground permits it. At the end of retention, make the record irrecoverable or de-identify it.
guide.do: A retention expiry creates a review and approved disposal task, not automatic deletion.
guide.when: At expiry, after holds and legal duties are checked
guide.keep: Retention schedule, hold check, approval and destruction certificate

Obligation: Protect personal data processed or stored outside Uganda

guide.what: Before using an overseas cloud or service provider, confirm equivalent protection or valid customer consent, document the transfer and bind the provider to the required security and confidentiality controls.
guide.do: Block vendor activation until the transfer basis and contract are approved.
guide.keep: Transfer assessment, country review, consent where used and contract

Obligation: Maintain FIA registration as an accountable person
Legal clock: As required by AML Act/Regulations and FIA registration process
Source / provision: AML Act Cap.118 s.21(pb)-(pc); AML Regulations regs.3-4; FIA Online Registration Guidelines 2024, section 11.4

guide.what: Money Lenders and microfinance institutions licensed in the Tier 4 sector fall within FIA accountable-person registration requirements.
guide.do: Store FIA registration status/number in Profile & registrations; create an action if registration is missing or current details change.
guide.when: As required by AML Act/Regulations and FIA registration process
guide.keep: FIA registration confirmation/number, registration forms and supporting licence/incorporation documents

Obligation: Appoint an MLCO and maintain an authorised goAML reporting account
Legal clock: Before reports need to be filed; update as required
Source / provision: AML Regulations MLCO provisions; FIA goAML guidance

guide.what: An accountable person should have a designated AML compliance function/MLCO and must be able to submit regulatory reports through FIA’s reporting system.
guide.do: Store MLCO and goAML status in Profile & registrations. A change of MLCO creates an update workflow.
guide.when: Before reports need to be filed; update as required
guide.keep: Appointment, FIA/goAML authorisation and current user/account record

Obligation: Maintain an approved AML/CFT compliance programme and submit the AML policy to FIA
Legal clock: Maintain continuously; FIA guidance requires policy submission
Source / provision: FIA Guidance Notes - AML Program and AML Policy

guide.what: The accountable person needs an AML/CFT programme with internal policies, procedures and controls, a compliance function, training and independent audit.
guide.do: Keep board/management approval, current policy version and FIA submission/feedback together; changes trigger a controlled update.
guide.when: Maintain continuously; FIA guidance requires policy submission
guide.keep: AML policy/programme, approval, FIA submission, feedback and implementation evidence

Obligation: Conduct and document the institutional ML/TF risk assessment and submit the results to FIA
Legal clock: Copy of results to FIA within 48 hours after conducting the risk assessment

guide.what: The accountable person must regularly identify, assess, monitor, manage and mitigate its money-laundering and terrorism-financing risks.
guide.do: Create an occurrence when the assessment is approved/completed and start the 48-hour submission clock from completion.
guide.when: Copy of results to FIA within 48 hours after conducting the risk assessment
guide.keep: Risk assessment, approval, FIA submission and receipt

Obligation: Assess ML/TF risk before launching a new product, delivery mechanism or technology
Behaviour: Prior assessment and event-driven regulatory report
Legal clock: Assessment before launch; copy of results to FIA within 48 hours after conducting the assessment
Source / provision: AML Act s.6A; AML Regulations reg.9

guide.what: A new product, business practice, delivery mechanism or technology must be assessed for ML/TF risk before launch.
guide.do: Make AML risk assessment a release gate; once assessment is completed, generate the 48-hour FIA submission task.
guide.when: Assessment before launch; copy of results to FIA within 48 hours after conducting the assessment
guide.keep: Product risk assessment, approval, FIA submission and release evidence

Obligation: Perform risk-based CDD/KYC and identify beneficial owners before or during the relationship as permitted by law
Legal clock: Before/while establishing the relationship or transaction as permitted by the AML framework
Source / provision: AML Act s.6; AML Regulations regs.13-19 and beneficial-owner provisions

guide.what: CDD must identify and verify the customer, authorised representatives and beneficial owners, understand ownership/control and the purpose/nature of the relationship, and be risk-based.
guide.do: No disbursement/relationship activation until required CDD is complete or a legally permitted deferred-verification case is documented.
guide.when: Before/while establishing the relationship or transaction as permitted by the AML framework
guide.keep: Identity/verification, beneficial-owner evidence, purpose/nature, risk rating and approval

Obligation: Apply enhanced due diligence to PEPs and other high-risk customers/transactions
Legal clock: Before establishing/continuing the relationship as required; then ongoing
Source / provision: AML Act s.6; AML Regulations regs.15 and 29

guide.what: High-risk cases require enhanced measures. PEP relationships require appropriate risk systems, senior-management approval, source-of-wealth/source-of-funds measures and enhanced ongoing monitoring.
guide.do: High-risk classification creates an EDD workflow and approval gate; retain source checks and ongoing monitoring plan.
guide.when: Before establishing/continuing the relationship as required; then ongoing
guide.keep: Risk assessment, EDD pack, PEP screening, source-of-wealth/funds evidence and approval

Obligation: Conduct ongoing customer due diligence, transaction monitoring and risk-based customer refresh
Source / provision: AML Act s.6; AML Regulations regs.15 and 17

guide.what: CDD does not end at onboarding. The lender should monitor transactions/relationships and keep identification and risk information current according to risk.
guide.do: Use monitoring alerts and risk-based review dates; each alert/refresh is an occurrence with evidence and disposition.
guide.keep: Monitoring alerts, customer refresh, risk-rating changes and dispositions

Obligation: Report suspicious transactions and attempted transactions to FIA within two working days of forming suspicion
Legal clock: Without delay and not later than 2 working days from the date suspicion was formed

guide.what: Where the lender suspects or has reasonable grounds to suspect money laundering or terrorism financing, it must file an STR regardless of transaction value and must not tip off the customer.
guide.do: Record the suspicion-formed timestamp, escalate to MLCO immediately, file via goAML within two working days and restrict access to the case.
guide.when: Without delay and not later than 2 working days from the date suspicion was formed
guide.keep: Internal alert/case, STR submission and receipt; access/tipping-off controls

Obligation: Report large cash/monetary transactions at or above the statutory threshold through the current FIA reporting cycle
Legal clock: Use the current FIA LCTR submission instruction/reporting cycle; do not invent a fixed day in FITSPA Compliance Platform
Source / provision: AML Act s.8; FIA reporting/goAML guidance

guide.what: Accountable persons must report cash/monetary transactions meeting the statutory large-cash threshold. FIA guidance identifies one thousand currency points as UGX 20,000,000.
guide.do: Transaction matching threshold creates an LCTR occurrence and routes it into the currently configured FIA reporting cycle.
guide.when: Use the current FIA LCTR submission instruction/reporting cycle; do not invent a fixed day in FITSPA Compliance Platform
guide.keep: Transaction record, threshold logic, LCTR submission and receipt

Obligation: Keep AML/CFT customer, transaction, report and enquiry records for the required retention period and make them retrievable
Legal clock: At least 10 years under the AML framework/FIA guidance
Source / provision: AML Act s.7; AML Regulations reg.28; FIA Guidance Notes

guide.what: AML records must allow transactions and decisions to be reconstructed and be available to competent authorities. FIA guidance states a ten-year record-keeping period.
guide.do: Map AML record classes to the retention schedule and suspend destruction where a legal/regulatory hold applies.
guide.when: At least 10 years under the AML framework/FIA guidance
guide.keep: Retention schedule, archive logs, reconstruction tests and legal holds

Obligation: Screen relevant staff, maintain regular AML training and keep evidence of competence
Source / provision: FIA Guidance Notes - AML Program / regular AML training

guide.what: The AML programme should include fit/integrity controls for relevant staff and ongoing training for employees and senior management.
guide.do: Maintain staff screening and training records; use a management-approved training calendar rather than calling it a statutory annual deadline unless FIA directs otherwise.
guide.keep: Screening checks, training materials, attendance and assessment records

Obligation: Maintain an independent AML audit function and track remediation
Legal clock: No single fixed statutory annual day identified in the validated sources; use approved audit plan or FIA instruction
Source / provision: FIA Guidance Notes - independent audit function / AML audit reports

guide.what: The AML compliance programme should be independently tested for effectiveness and weaknesses should be remediated.
guide.do: Schedule from the approved AML audit plan; create regulator submission task only where FIA/current instruction requires it.
guide.when: No single fixed statutory annual day identified in the validated sources; use approved audit plan or FIA instruction
guide.keep: Audit report, management response, action tracker and submission evidence where required

Obligation: Screen for targeted financial sanctions and implement freezing/reporting measures when required
Legal clock: Immediately/as required by the applicable sanctions direction/guideline
Source / provision: FIA Targeted Financial Sanctions Guidelines; AML/CFT statutes

guide.what: Accountable persons must have measures to identify designated persons/entities and implement applicable freezing and reporting obligations under Uganda’s targeted-financial-sanctions framework.
guide.do: Run screening at onboarding and ongoing. Potential matches create restricted-access review; confirmed matches trigger the prescribed freeze/report steps.
guide.when: Immediately/as required by the applicable sanctions direction/guideline
guide.keep: Screening logs, match analysis, freeze/action record and notices/reports

Obligation: Apply the current FIA high-risk-jurisdiction controls on a risk-sensitive basis
Source / provision: AML Regulations reg.44; current FIA high-risk-jurisdiction circular

guide.what: FIA periodically circulates FATF high-risk/increased-monitoring updates. The product must use the current circular rather than a static country list.
guide.do: Maintain the active FIA circular/version and apply proportionate controls; do not hard-code a permanent jurisdiction list.
guide.keep: Current circular, jurisdiction screening, risk assessment and additional measures

Obligation: Report international wire transfers where the lender itself carries out a reportable international wire transfer
Applies to: Both - if international wire transfers are conducted
Legal clock: Use the current FIA international-wire reporting instruction/cycle
Source / provision: FIA International Wire Transfer Reporting Guidelines

guide.what: FIA International Wire Transfer Reporting guidance treats transfers with a source or destination outside Uganda as reportable irrespective of amount.
guide.do: Do not ask this at initial setup unless relevant. Detect/log the transaction and create the report occurrence if the lender conducts such transfers.
guide.when: Use the current FIA international-wire reporting instruction/cycle
guide.keep: Transfer details, IWTR submission and receipt

Obligation: Document and evidence the lender's own sources of funds
Legal clock: Before reliance/use as internally approved; regulator deadline where requested

guide.what: A digital credit provider must provide the regulator with evidence and sources of funds invested or proposed to be invested in the digital credit provider.
guide.do: Link each material funding source to approval and supporting evidence; create regulator submission occurrence when requested.
guide.when: Before reliance/use as internally approved; regulator deadline where requested
guide.keep: Funding agreements, bank evidence, source/beneficial-owner checks and regulator submission
